title: terraform: private modules — GPU node pools, IAM, networking, and state layout refactor
author: Asha Patel
description: Refactor and extend the Terraform modules used by Private deployments to support configurable GPU node pools, clearer IAM role boundaries, deterministic networking resources, and an improved backend/state layout for easier upgrades and drift recovery. Motivation: customers deploying Private (VPC/on-prem) with GPU workloads hit recurring issues around node pool scaling, mixed-privilege IAM policies, and statefile lock scoping across environments. This change introduces: 1) a new `gpu_node_pool` module with explicit GPU type, taints/tolerations, and autoscaling policies; 2) split IAM role modules to separate runtime, observability, and admin privileges (least-privilege defaults); 3) deterministic networking layout with shared subnets and clearer NAT/egress rules and optional BGP routes for on-prem interconnects; 4) reorganized remote state layout and locking keys so per-environment and per-cluster statefiles are isolated and easier to migrate. Backwards compatibility: modules provide input variables with sensible defaults and migration helpers in docs. There is an upgrade plan section with example `terraform state mv` commands and a deprecation period for legacy resource names. Tests: unit tf validate/fmt, plan diffs against existing test fixtures, and an integration smoke test deploying to a staging VPC with a single GPU node pool. See checklist: - docs updated with migration guide - automated plan check for existing customers - preserved legacy outputs (shim variables) for two releases - security review completed

release_notes: Refactors Private deployment Terraform modules: adds gpu_node_pool module, splits IAM roles for least privilege, introduces deterministic networking with optional BGP, and changes remote state layout.
